adjudication.rationale: Third report of the same fact as R11-675 (ledger 704ebe904f59951e) and R11-674: `LbAssertion` carries no audience and no ingress identity (v1.rs:52-64), `signing_preimage` binds exactly those four fields (v1.rs:86-99), and `verify` (v1.rs:218-262) has no audience arm, where v2 added one (`AudienceMismatch`, v2.rs:357-358, enforced at v2.rs:531-534). Confirmed, and confirmed also that it is not a fixable line: the format is frozen by ADR-MCPS-023 §C1 (stated at v1.rs:5-7) and Mode B is refused as a RULING about the LB's place in the TCB (config_state/transport.rs:184-191, ingress/mod.rs:18-19). The suggested disposition — read `GUARANTEE` as 'request-bound, not node-bound' — is the same documentation fix recorded on R11-675.

title: A v1 assertion is scoped to a request but not to a node

adjudication.rationale: The cross-node fact is real and source-verified: `LbAssertion` has four fields (v1.rs:52-64), `signing_preimage` covers exactly `key_id`, `asserted_client_identity`, `request_hash`, `validation_time` (v1.rs:86-99), and `verify` (v1.rs:218-262) has no audience or node arm — v2 added `audience` for precisely this and refuses on mismatch (v2.rs:357-358, 531-534). So any node trusting the same LB key id accepts an assertion minted for a sibling node, for the same request bytes, within `max_age_secs`. It is not a fixable line: the v1 format is FROZEN by ADR-MCPS-023 §C1 (v1.rs:5-7) and Mode B is refused as a ruling about the LB's place in the trusted computing base, not as a gap (config_state/transport.rs:184-191, ingress/mod.rs:18-19). What over-reaches is the replay note at v1.rs:209-217, which discharges same-request replay to 'that request's OWN replay protection' — a per-node cache that says nothing across nodes — and the contract's `does_not_own`, which lists only the absent nonce. This is where two honest facts state a false relation, so the work is to record the limit, not to add a check.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Record the limit where the format's honesty is stated — the `# Honesty boundary` at v1.rs:45-51 and the `# Replay` note at v1.rs:209-217: a v1 assertion is request-bound but NOT node-bound, so any node trusting the same LB key id admits it for the same request bytes, and the per-node replay cache does not close that; v2's `audience` is the concrete difference. Add the same line to the contract's `does_not_own`, which today names only the absent nonce.

title: The v1 ingress assertion binds no audience, so it is valid at every node trusting the same LB key

adjudication.rationale: Verified in both verifiers: `pub fn with_max_age_secs(mut self, max_age_secs: i64) -> Self` bounds nothing (v1.rs:171-175, v2.rs:429-433), and the freshness test is `age.saturating_abs() > self.max_age_secs` (v1.rs:255, v2.rs:514), so `i64::MAX` makes it unsatisfiable and disables freshness in both directions; a negative value refuses everything, so the danger is one-directional as stated. v1 genuinely has no other temporal limit — no `expires_at`, no audience, no ingress-identity allowlist (`LbAssertion` is four fields, v1.rs:52-64). It is embedder-reachable, not merely internal: `pub mod transport` (lib.rs:200), `pub mod ingress` (transport/mod.rs:34), both binding types `pub`. Severity stays low because nothing reaches it — `with_max_age_secs` has ZERO callers anywhere in the workspace, and both modes are refused at Layer-A (config_state/transport.rs:184-191 and 287-298). The in-repo precedent the finding names is real and is the right shape: `VerifierPolicy::MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_BOUND = 300` (mcp-re-http-profile/src/policy.rs:113) is refused at construction in `VerifierPolicy::new` (policy.rs:151). ingress/mod.rs:23-25 is explicit that an unreached check is not a reason to weaken one.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Bound the window where it is set. `LbAssertionBinding::with_max_age_secs` (v1.rs:172) and `LbAssertionV2Binding::with_max_age_secs` (v2.rs:430) should refuse a non-positive or implausibly large value the way `VerifierPolicy::new` refuses a skew outside `0..=MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_BOUND`, so a verifier that exists has a freshness window the replay argument at v1.rs:209-217 / v2.rs:480-485 can actually assume.

title: `with_max_age_secs` accepts any window, including one that disables freshness entirely

adjudication.rationale: Same lines, same mechanism and same fix as R11-672 (ledger 8f8607547e2f401d): `with_max_age_secs` is `pub`, takes any `i64`, and `i64::MAX` makes `age.saturating_abs() > self.max_age_secs` unsatisfiable (v1.rs:171-175 / 255, v2.rs:429-433 / 514). adjudication.rationale: Both halves check out, and the v1 half is the sharper one. v2: `parse` bounds the whole wire at `MAX_V2_ASSERTION_WIRE_LEN = 64 * 1024` (v2_wire.rs:23, 80), applies `validate_asserted_identity_value` to `asserted_client_identity` only (v2_wire.rs:112), and gives `key_id`, `ingress_identity`, `request_hash` and `audience` nothing but non-empty + no-control-character (v2_wire.rs:117-121); all of them enter the preimage (v2.rs:211-220) that is hashed and Ed25519-verified at v2.rs:499-506, before any of it is trusted. That is bounded work, so on its own it is hardening. v1 is the opposite error and it is a correctness bug, not hardening: v1_wire.rs:36 bounds the ENTIRE five-field wire by `MAX_ASSERTED_IDENTITY_LEN`, which is `MAX_PEER_IDENTITY_LEN = 8192` (communication_assurance/peer_identity_value.rs:27) — the identity's OWN ceiling — while the wire base64url-expands every field by 4/3 and appends an 86-character signature. So an identity anywhere near the 8192-byte value the identity validator accepts cannot be carried in a legal v1 assertion at all; it fails as `Malformed`, which is a false refusal rather than a refusal of anything hostile.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Give each field a ceiling that means something for that field in both parsers. In `v2_wire::parse` (v2_wire.rs:117-121) bound `key_id`, `ingress_identity`, `request_hash` and `audience` individually instead of leaving them to whatever the 64 KiB shared budget allows. In `v1_wire::parse` (v1_wire.rs:36) replace the identity ceiling reused as a total-wire bound with a v1 wire ceiling that admits a maximum-length identity plus its four sibling fields' base64url expansion and the signature.

adjudication.rationale: The neighbouring primitive disproves it. `verify_ed25519_with` calls `key.inner.verify_strict(...)` at `mcp-re-core/src/crypto.rs:191`, with the comment at `:190` stating exactly the property — `verify_strict` rejects weak/small-order public keys and non-canonical encodings (ed25519-dalek 3.0.0, `Cargo.lock:475-478`). So a credential whose `cnf.jwk.x` is a small-order or all-zero point parses into a `VerificationKey` but authorizes nothing: every step-8 response-signature check under it refuses. The degenerate key is accepted as a PARSE and refused as a VERIFIER, which is the fail-closed outcome, and ASM-0027 (`verification/policy/assumptions.toml:624-635`) is the premise over exactly this call.

notes: Undecided inside its packet; needs mcp-re-client-core ClientVerification::DelegatedRequired and its RevocationSource — the owner of DL-08

adjudication.rationale: No ASM covers the revocation seam — I read every `id`/`description` pair in `verification/policy/assumptions.toml` and the only revocation entry is ASM-0038 (X.509 CRL index keys, `unit://proxy.credential_currency`). But the graph does not need one, because no claim rests on the seam being right: THM-0058 is worded 'a credential whose issuer kid, delegated kid or jti THE TRUST AUTHORITY REPORTS revoked resolves nothing' (`verification/policy/theorems.toml:2700-2703`), and THM-0057's scope explicitly disclaims completeness — 'or that a revocation list is complete' (`theorems.toml:2686-2688`). The premise the finding wants registered is one the theorems already decline to make. Operationally there is also no seam that can fail to answer: the only production `RevocationSource` impls are `StaticRevocationList` (`mcp-re-client-core/src/delegated_trust/revocation.rs:83-88`) and `TrustedIssuerSet` (`delegated_trust/anchors.rs:191`), both total in-memory denylists, and the trait doc already states the conservative rule for a future networked source (`revocation.rs:29-32`).

adjudication.rationale: The ordering is correct at main — `check_root_signature` runs first at verify.rs:181, with `check_freshness`/`check_scope`/`check_epoch_and_revocation` at 183-185 and the comment `Every step below reads values the root has signed` at 182 — and nothing measures it. I re-derived the swap by hand over every negative test in delegation/mod.rs::tests: each mutates exactly one field over an otherwise well-formed, correctly root-signed credential, so `wrong_alg` (323), `wrong_typ` (335), `unknown_issuer_is_untrusted` (359), `expired_and_not_yet_valid` (373), all four scope tests (442-491), the epoch test (494) and both revocation tests (514, 526) return the identical verdict whichever order the four calls are in. `bad_root_signature_is_credential_invalid` (mod.rs:347-356) mints with an untrusted root but supplies GOOD claims, so a verifier that ran the cheap checks first would still reach the signature check and still answer `DelegationCredentialInvalid`. The one credential that would discriminate — invalid under BOTH the root signature and a later step, asserting the signature's verdict — does not exist anywhere in the crate. The contract's `code-reading-only` label for G8 is honest, so this is a missing control rather than an overstated claim; the reviewer's refusal-token-oracle story is a consequence of a hypothetical future reorder, not of main, which is why I revise the severity down.
adjudication.smallest_fix: One control in `mcp-re-http-profile/src/delegation/mod.rs::tests`: mint a credential with an untrusted root AND an out-of-scope `mcp_re_audience_hash` (or a stale `trust_epoch`), and assert the verdict is `DelegationCredentialInvalid` rather than `DelegationAudienceMismatch` / `DelegationTrustEpochStale`. That single case fails if any of the three later checks is hoisted above `check_root_signature`.

adjudication.rationale: The arithmetic is as described and it is the CORRECT arithmetic; what is wrong is the sentence the operator reads. mcp-re-http-profile/src/pdp_decision/verify.rs:130 enforces `now.saturating_sub(iat) > max_decision_age.saturating_add(skew)`, and the same `skew` widens `[nbf, exp]` two lines up (:117-119) — which is right, because `iat` is on the ISSUER's clock and `now` is on the verifier's, so without the term a decision issued by a lagging issuer would be born partly stale. capability.rs:74-77 gives exactly that reason for reusing the deployment's single `--max-clock-skew`, and the widening is bounded: `VerifierPolicy::MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_BOUND = 300` (mcp-re-http-profile/src/policy.rs:113) is enforced at startup (app.rs:738-749), so the true cap is `--authz-max-decision-age-secs + at most 300s`, not an open window. The defect is that the ON line at capability.rs:60-69 advertises only the first term — 'decisions accepted up to {}s old' — and `PdpDecisionFreshness::max_decision_age`'s own doc at verify.rs:57-60 calls itself 'the verifier's own cap on how old a decision it will act on', which is short by up to the skew. With replay of a decision deliberately not owned (a Permit authorizes unboundedly many requests inside its window), the window's advertised width is the operator's only handle on reuse, so the transcript should not understate it. The reviewer's alternative — decide staleness against the cap alone — would make the two freshness gates disagree about clock tolerance, which is the thing capability.rs:74-77 exists to prevent; the transcript is the right place to fix.
adjudication.smallest_fix: In `mcp-re-proxy/src/authorization/capability.rs`, make the ON line (:60-69) state the enforced bound rather than one of its two terms — e.g. 'decisions accepted up to {age}s old, plus the {skew}s clock-skew tolerance' — and correct the `max_decision_age` field doc at mcp-re-http-profile/src/pdp_decision/verify.rs:57-60 to say it is the cap BEFORE skew is applied. No change to the comparison at verify.rs:130.

title: The deployment's RFC 9421 clock skew silently widens the decision staleness cap

adjudication.rationale: The absence is real: `delegated_key` checks only `kty`, `crv` and `jwk.kid == claims.delegated_kid` (verify.rs:155-161), `check_root_signature` checks only `header.kid == claims.issuer_kid` (verify.rs:54-56), and nothing anywhere compares the delegated key against the root it just resolved. A root-signed credential attesting the root's own key therefore verifies and is handed back as the response-signing key in `VerifiedDelegation` (verify.rs:187-195). There is no unprivileged path — a root that mints such a credential could mint anything — and this deployment's producer cannot do it, because `delegated_kid` is the RFC 7638 thumbprint of a key the factory mints fresh on every issuance (custody/mod.rs:434-469, delegated_wiring.rs:114-118). The value of the check is that it is the verifier-side statement of the hot/cold separation the whole design rests on, which the module doc calls load-bearing rather than defence in depth (verify.rs:4-7): a deployment that misconfigures its issuer to delegate to itself puts the root key on the request path with no signal at all. One correction to the proposed fix: compare the MATERIALIZED keys, not the kid strings — a kid is a locator, and two names for one key would pass a string comparison.
adjudication.smallest_fix: In `mcp-re-http-profile/src/delegation/verify.rs`, have `verify_delegation_credential` refuse `DelegationCredentialInvalid` when the `VerificationKey` materialized from `cnf.jwk` equals the root `VerificationKey` `resolve_root` returned for `claims.issuer_kid` — a byte comparison of the two materialized points, not of `delegated_kid` against `issuer_kid`. That needs the resolved root threaded out of `check_root_signature` or the comparison moved beside it.

This row's extra observation is accurate and worth carrying into the fix: the only bound on `T` anywhere is `cadence_violations`, and it derives the cadence ceiling FROM `t_secs` (config_state/trust_revocation.rs:346-352), so a larger `T` buys a looser cadence rather than being constrained by anything.

title: No wired ceiling on T: bounded-cache:86400 validates and prints a 172800s window with no warning

adjudication.rationale: The third statement of the same gap: `RECOMMENDED_MAX_T_SECS` / `t_exceeds_recommended_max` carry `#[allow(dead_code)]` with no caller, and `strictest_applicable_t` has no production input because `ApplicableClassWindows` can only be built empty (window_policy.rs:40-51, :98-109). Folded into R11-736 (ledger e9847bb3d19832e8). title: No upper bound on T is ever enforced or even warned about

adjudication.rationale: The finding bundles two dormant items that must be adjudicated apart, and only one is a defect. `strictest_applicable_t` is a POSITIVE CONTROL: `ApplicableClassWindows` has exactly one production constructor and it is empty (window_policy.rs:98-109), so the ADR-MCPS-021 'strictest applicable T' rule is the identity BY TYPE, and the module says what would have to arrive before it is wired — a request classifier and a per-class deployment input — and refuses to fabricate the second (:93-97). That is this repo's own stated handling of dormant code and adding configuration to activate it would be the defect. `t_exceeds_recommended_max` is different in kind: it needs NO missing input. `T` is already in hand on the line where the operator reads the window — `RevocationTier::startup_audit_line` (revocation_tier.rs:169-175) and `delivered_revocation_window` (delivered_window.rs:66-72) both have it — so this is an advisory ADR-MCPS-021 asks for, that costs one comparison, and that nothing performs (:40-51, `#[allow(dead_code)]`, zero callers). Concretely: `--revocation-tier bounded-cache:86400` with a matching 86400s cadence passes `cadence_violations` (whose ceiling IS `t_secs`, config_state/trust_revocation.rs:346-352) and the proxy prints a 172800s delivered window with no annotation of any kind. The module documents the gap honestly, which is why this is low rather than higher, but a documented gap is still a gap.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Wire `t_exceeds_recommended_max` onto the surface that already prints the number — append the annotation to `delivered_revocation_window`'s string when the tier's `T` exceeds `RECOMMENDED_MAX_T_SECS`, since that is the one sentence an operator sizes an incident response from and it already holds `t_secs`. That removes the `#[allow(dead_code)]` on the predicate and its constant; leave `strictest_applicable_t` and `ApplicableClassWindows` exactly as they are, and say in the module doc that the advisory is now wired and the selector still is not, so the two dormancies stop reading as one.

adjudication.rationale: The code is right and the claim is not. Every one of the five remote-signer request sites applies the constant: `aws_kms_keysource.rs:195`, `aws_sts.rs:622`, `gcp_kms_keysource.rs:456`, `:749`, `:771`, all `.timeout(NETWORK_TIMEOUT)`. adjudication.smallest_fix: Two corrections, neither a redesign. (1) Fix `credential_egress.rs:66-68`: the timeout is NOT what bounds a call; each request's own `.timeout(..)` is. adjudication.rationale: The predicate is what the finding says and no neighbouring source justifies it. `self_issued` is pure Name-DER equality (x509_adapter.rs:70) and `issuer_validity_refusal` skips the per-request window for any non-leaf certificate carrying that shape (evaluation.rs:153). The registry declines to cover the decision: ASM-0038 states 'Equality of the two `Name` encodings is trusted only as a REPORTED SHAPE. What a self-issued certificate is exempt from is `evaluation`'s decision, not the parser's, and this premise does not reach it' (assumptions.toml:1060-1063). The justification written in the code (x509_adapter.rs:29-32, evaluation.rs:564-566) is about a peer sending its ROOT, but the predicate admits any self-issued certificate, including a cross-certified intermediate -- and this per-request window check exists precisely because a resumed session skips chain building (resumption_binding.rs:26-34), so an expired self-issued intermediate in a stored chain is re-admitted on every request.

ActiveDelegatedKey::issued refuses with a typed custody::IssuanceRefusal: RootKeyMismatch when the configured root public key, under the configured issuer kid, did not sign the credential (root_signed's refusal), NotAsRequested when the root signed a credential that does not attest this issuance; the custody records RootUnavailable when the issuer seam returns nothing, keeps the cause as last_refusal() (cleared on adoption), and DelegatedRotor::last_refusal projects it. signing_plane renders it on the rotation warnings (mint_successor::back_off_after_failure) and the startup refusal as `cause=<token>: ...`, the mismatch as `cause=root-key-mismatch: root issuer CONTRACT VIOLATION ...`; no message-text matching. Security outcome unchanged: nothing published, predecessor serves to its exp, then fail closed. Evidence: custody::tests::the_refusal_cause_tells_an_outage_from_a_root_signing_under_another_key, the three active_key refusal tests asserting the typed cause, signing_plane::rotation_owner_tests::a_startup_refusal_tells_an_offline_root_from_one_signing_under_another_key (a root advertising one key and signing with another, end to end through build_delegated_signing), mint_successor::tests::the_rotation_warning_names_the_cause_the_custody_kept; M490 (mismatch collapsed into RootUnavailable) and M491 (rendered cause collapsed) red; M477 re-anchored, red. Theorem review states unchanged (97/17/15/4). Previously: Found beside B4b (2618b0d1). Before it, delegated_wiring::root_signature re-verified the root's signature and eprintln'd 'issuance refused: root issuer CONTRACT VIOLATION ...' before returning None. The check now lives in ActiveDelegatedKey::issued (the verifier's check_root_signature), whose Err attempt_issuance discards with .ok(), so a root signing under a key it does not advertise fails closed exactly as before but leaves only signing_plane's generic 'delegated key issuance FAILED (root issuer unavailable)' line. Fail-closed behaviour is unchanged; what is lost is the operator's ability to tell an outage from a misconfigured root. Nature: observability, not a bypass.
title: An issuance the root did not sign is refused silently: the operator sees only the generic root-unavailable rotation warning, not which contract the root broke

notes: Owner ruling 28.3: residual of fb29f893's one-past-the-mark repair (4372a575), not accepted. Two cases absorb an operator's intended rotation: (1) replicas hold different high-water marks when the shared counter rolls back; a repair from the lower mark can land the counter EQUAL to a higher replica's mark, which then reads no regression and keeps its pre-rollback label (test a_repair_from_a_lower_mark_can_land_on_a_higher_replicas_label, epoch_watch.rs:31-36); (2) a raw operator INCR that brings the rolled-back key back to exactly an already-seen mark before any replica reads it is indistinguishable from no rollback (epoch_watch.rs:36-38). Clients accept by their static accepted_epochs, so a compromised credential is not kept acceptable once its label is dropped; the defect is an absorbed rotation and an avoidable fleet outage when clients drop the label. Target design (ruling 28.3): replace raw INCR with one atomic domain operation that advances the authoritative epoch strictly past every epoch already acknowledged by the authority; a durable repair-generation/floor key is acceptable. a90c2fb9 + 1fe2c504: FIXED (owner ruling 30, option a). `mcp-re-proxy trust-epoch advance` (mcp-re-proxy/src/trust_epoch/advance.rs) draws a 128-bit generation with getrandom::fill BEFORE any write (a failed draw refuses with nothing written; no fallback generation), then one EVAL INCRs the counter and SETs `<key>:generation` beside it. DelegatedEpochWatch reads counter+generation in one MGET; a generation it has not accounted for on a counter equal to its mark is refused (EpochRefusal::Reused) and the counter moved one past the mark via the forward-only raise, the generation accounted only once the store is past the mark, so both cases end strictly beyond every reading replica's mark: (1) an advance repaired from a lower mark onto a higher replica's label (test an_advance_repaired_onto_a_higher_replicas_label_still_ends_past_it, replacing the test that demonstrated the defect), (2) an advance bringing the rolled-back key back to exactly the mark (an_advance_back_to_the_mark_ends_past_it; live epoch_watch::live::an_advance_back_to_the_mark_is_moved_past_it). Unchanged counter+generation is no advance (an_unchanged_counter_and_generation_is_not_an_advance); a failed repair stays refused (an_unrepaired_advance_on_the_mark_stays_refused). No floor key: acknowledged epochs live in replica marks and a floor in the same store rolls back with the counter. Raw INCR carries no generation and is documented as unsupported (fleet guide, NOTES.txt, values.yaml); whole-fleet restart limitation unchanged (f6d3d0d1). Probes M515 (generation check dropped), M516 (generation accounted before repair), M517 (failed draw still advances) red; M448/M500-M502 re-anchored and red. ASM-0068 re-signed at six sites (Ruling 30). Live: trust_epoch::advance::live (2) and epoch_watch::live (2) passed against Redis 7 locally; wired into live-infra-e2e.yml.
title: A trust-epoch rollback can absorb an operator's rotation: a repair from a lower mark or a raw INCR to an already-seen mark leaves a replica on its pre-rollback label

notes: Found in the L-EPOCH follow-up (a90c2fb9 added a per-advance generation). TrustEpochSource::poll_once compared only the counter with the last value it saw, so a store rolled back and then advanced (mcp-re-proxy trust-epoch advance) back onto that counter between two polls, or during an outage, read as no change and queued no FlushAll: a push-tier revocation then took effect only by bounded-T expiry, not within one poll interval as the push tier states. Severity low: the bounded-T fallback still caps the window, and the advance's other consumer (DelegatedEpochWatch) already accounts the generation. bccd3ed4: FIXED. The poller reads EpochState (counter + generation, one MGET) and flushes when either differs; EpochReader::read_state is the one read, read_epoch its projection. Test an_advance_onto_an_already_seen_counter_still_flushes under proxy.trust_epoch_source; probe M518 compares the counter alone and turns it red (verify-mutations PASS); M97 re-anchored and PASS.
title: The trust plane's push flush keyed on the epoch counter alone, so an advance onto an already-seen counter after a store rollback did not flush the trust cache

notes: Found by the Ruling 33 authority-closure review of THM-0063. DelegatedSigningCustody::sign_response (public) read the delegated key directly through the *_with_owned_key emitter and clamped `expires` with its own copy of the validity relation (issuance_terms::signature_valid_until) instead of opening a SigningWindow, contradicting THM-0063's 'the emitters that read it take a window'. The advertised validity was identical and the production proxy does not call it, so no signature advertised excess validity; the defect was a second statement of the relation and a public emitter outside the window. Ruling 34 §2: it now opens SigningWindow::over and signs through window_emission::sign_delegated_response_full; signature_valid_until is deleted; no window (non-positive TTL, credential past exp) is refused with CustodyError::NoSigningWindow.
title: DelegatedSigningCustody::sign_response signed with the delegated key outside a SigningWindow

title: The delegated trust-epoch startup banner told operators a raw INCR advances the fleet

notes: Ruling 34 §7 A. theorem_assurance compared only the theorem's own claim fingerprint, so 23+ theorems (THM-0007 on ASM-0062/0063, THM-0041 on ASM-0065, ...) read REVIEWED while premises under them changed unsigned; the unit axis carried the assumption digest but a re-measured unit is FRESH on a premise nobody signed. theorem_assurance now takes each theorem's premise closure (_fingerprint.theorem_premises: the supporting units' trusted_assumptions plus every assumption scoped to a boundary those units cross) and a `review` verdict that is REVIEWED only when the claim's review and every premise's assumption-axis review hold at the current digest and are ledger-backed; `established` requires it. Measured at landing: 55 of 133 theorems REVIEWED (claim and premises), 43 PREMISE_UNREVIEWED; 64 assumptions block, most never recorded on the assumption axis.
title: A theorem read REVIEWED while an assumption in its premise closure had no owner approval at its current digest

notes: Ruling 34 §7 B. A claim-correction record whose packet is docs/security/owner-approvals-*.jsonl passed when the file existed; no gate read the ledger, and assumption/specification review records were never cross-checked against an owner signature. tools/verification/_approvals.py now loads the ledger and refuses it whole if any line's sha256 is not the digest of its text; an ENTRY approval (source names one registry entry) backs that entry only at the exact text it signs. Correction records must find a ledger line naming the subject (or, for a dependency correction, a premise in its depends_on closure), and an own-claim correction must match the subject's entry approval field for field. An assumption premise is backed only by an entry approval at its current text; a specification record is refuted by an entry approval at other text. Found while landing: the 2026-10-07 THM-0093 entry approval had captured THM-0094's entry as well; its text and sha256 are corrected to THM-0093's entry alone.
title: Owner-approval references were satisfied by a ledger file existing, not by what it signs

notes: Ruling 34 §7 C, NOT YET FIXED — scope measured, owner decision needed. Specification review records carry only the theorem fingerprint (claim, dependency claims, review requirement); a supporting unit's source, evidence or premises can move under a REVIEWED theorem, which is by design today (test_a_source_change_does_not_dirty_specification_review). Measured impact of binding REVIEWED to the supporting units' full current fingerprints (_fingerprint.fingerprint_unit): of 98 spec-REVIEWED theorems, 89 have a supporting unit whose declared paths changed since the review record's commit and 96 have paths or toolchains.lock.toml changed (the 2026-09-29 Bazel migration moved toolchain identity for every unit); only THM-0041 and THM-0134 would survive. Reconstructing reviewed-time unit fingerprints is not faithful: the unit fingerprint includes toolchain identity, Bazel dependency closure and policy revision, which the recording commit's tree cannot reproduce under the current encoding without a checkout. Options are in the Ruling 34 return. | 2026-10-07@ruling-35: be81a45e implements the two axes (Ruling 35 §3): specification records carry review_digest over claim, premises and the supporting units' SEMANTIC components; theorem_assurance reports review_current, evidence_established and currently_verified; regression tests cover claim, premise, implementation-source, test-selection, toolchain and proof-policy changes. STILL OPEN per Ruling 35 §5: no theorem is yet re-reviewed under the new digest (0 of 133 REVIEW_CURRENT), so current status does not yet reflect both axes truthfully for any theorem; closes after the one-time subsystem re-review.
title: A theorem's REVIEWED state does not depend on its supporting units' fingerprints

notes: Found in the Ruling 35 G4 re-review of THM-0105. Since 6e86fb53 the Redis and etcd stores expire a record on the replica clock held back by the declared divergence d, so they keep it until retain_until + d in true time, while AsyncReplayTier pruned its retention account on the verifier's bare reading and handed the charge back at retain_until. One actor could hold (W + d) / W times its budget in a noeviction store; weakened, not removed, and not a replay bypass. ReplicaClockDivergence::held_back is now the one statement of the padding: retention_clock reads through it and the tier reserves and prunes the account on held_back(now_unix).
title: The per-replica retention account handed a charge back before the shared store dropped the record it accounted for
